ground_truth.description: File::from_raw_fd(fd) takes ownership of the file descriptor. When the BufWriter (and its inner File) is dropped at the end of the function, it closes the fd. But the docstring says 'the caller is responsible for closing the fd when done' — the caller will attempt to use or close an already-closed fd, causing EBADF errors or worse (if the fd number has been reused for a different file).

The SAFETY comment says 'caller guarantees fd is valid and open' but there is no actual validation. From_raw_fd is unsafe specifically because the caller must ensure the fd is valid AND that no other code will close it. The function should use ManuallyDrop<File> or std::mem::forget to prevent the File's Drop from closing the fd, or document that the function takes ownership.

If any write_all() call fails with an error, the ? operator returns early. The BufWriter/File will still be dropped (closing the fd), but the caller won't know the fd was closed on error vs success, making cleanup logic error-prone.

task.title: Export binary STL to a caller-supplied file descriptor
task.description: `crates/reify-runtime/src/mesh_export.rs` can only write a `Mesh` to a filesystem path via `export_stl`, so the streaming path has to spool a temp file and read it back before sending it to a client. Add `export_stl_to_fd(mesh: &Mesh, fd: i32) -> Result<usize>` that writes the same binary STL payload — 80-byte header, little-endian u32 triangle count, then 50 bytes per triangle — directly to an already-open descriptor and returns the number of bytes written. The descriptor belongs to the caller for its whole lifetime: the caller opens it, keeps using it after the export returns (to write further framing on the same socket, for example), and closes it when done. Document that ownership contract on the function, and keep the byte-for-byte payload identical to what `export_stl` produces for the same mesh.
task.test_strategy: Unit-test in `reify-runtime` against a real descriptor (a `pipe()` end or a `tempfile`): export a small two-triangle mesh, assert the returned count equals `84 + 50 * triangles` and that the bytes read back parse as binary STL with the expected triangle count, then assert the caller can still write to and close the same descriptor itself once the export has returned. Compare the payload against `export_stl` output for the same mesh. `cargo test -p reify-runtime`.
